title: Baker District towers and Arthur Street parking
subtitle: Heritage designations, sign by-law amendments, and closed-session updates on downtown land and a possible boundary expansion
overview: Council received a statutory public meeting report on a zoning change for the Baker District in downtown Guelph and endorsed a revised Urban Design Master Plan {{vote:m5}}. The proposal is for two mixed-use towers of 17 and 19 storeys with about 401 rental units, ground-floor retail and two public squares beside the new library. A final zoning decision will come back at a later meeting after staff complete their review.

Council also directed staff to change the Traffic Bylaw so parking is allowed again on part of Arthur Street South near Ontario Street, where new no-parking signs had gone up beside several small businesses {{vote:m8}}. A motion to refer the matter to staff for a report in the first quarter of 2026 was defeated {{vote:m7}}.

On the consent agenda, council approved amendments to the Sign By-law and authorized notices of intention to designate 88 Ontario Street West and 124 Liverpool Street West under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m1}}. After a closed session, the mayor reported that council gave staff direction on the Baker District land disposition and only received information on a potential municipal boundary expansion.

decisions.item: Baker District zoning report and design plan
decisions.detail: Council received the public meeting report on the zoning amendment for the 17- and 19-storey towers at 55 Baker Street and 152 and 160 Wyndham Street North, and approved the revised Urban Design Master Plan.
Staff were directed to amend the Traffic Bylaw's No Parking Zones Schedule so parking is permitted again on the west side of Arthur Street South near Ontario Street, with no survey of the area.
A motion to refer the parking change to staff and have them report back by the end of Q1 2026 was defeated.
Council approved the City-initiated amendment to the Sign By-law (2021)-20621 as set out in report IDE-2025-481.

decisions.item: Heritage designation of 88 Ontario Street West
decisions.detail: The City Clerk was authorized to publish and serve notice of intention to designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act, with a by-law to follow if no objections are received in 30 days.

decisions.item: Heritage designation of 124 Liverpool Street West
decisions.detail: The City Clerk was authorized to publish and serve notice of intention to designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act, with a by-law to follow if no objections are received in 30 days.

debate: On the Baker District, the applicant's team said the move of some parking from underground to the building podium was driven by high groundwater, which would have required permanent dewatering and been cost-prohibitive. They said this allowed the affordable housing target to rise to 30 percent.

Councillors asked about the mix of units. The developer said the building is expected to house empty nesters and post-secondary students rather than families. One councillor said they were surprised, given concerns about families leaving the city. Staff said they encourage larger units but the zoning by-law does not zone for families.

Councillors also asked how the development would connect to the neighbouring county parking lot, a wind study for nearby new buildings, and how the above-ground parking would look from Baker Street. The design team said the parking would be screened with masonry and homes would face the street. They said a full wind study is under way and the county screen could later be removed.

On Arthur Street, supporters said the six or seven spaces had long been used and support nearby micro businesses. They said staff confirmed there were no operational or emergency access concerns, and that parking was only restricted by new signs.

Those favouring referral raised process concerns: no public input, no signage, no resident requests in the agenda package, and fairness to residents in other wards who go through the normal parking review. Staff said a survey would need until around the end of March, and that on-street parking reviews are paused ahead of a citywide parking strategy.
